absent: Full interrupt translation table entry layout beyond valid marking and low power identifier association.
Internals of device register and unregister plus table write and cache invalidate and controller sync primitives.
Translate base discovery and platform message preparation through the IOMMU layer.
Wire bridge register offsets and identification and control field encodings and idle status definition.
Global controller data layout and low power domain creation and sizing.
Complete hardware interrupt initialisation beyond the truncated fragment ending mid function.
Parent chip and parent domain operation semantics for mask and unmask and affinity and state.
ACPI translator and translate frame structure layouts and IORT token registration semantics.
Message descriptor and allocation info layouts including cookie and scratchpad conventions.
CPU interface capability detection and private peripheral system register definitions.

findings.text: The ITS message layer publishes prepare and teardown operations for use by the message core. Prepare builds a per device context for a requested vector count and records platform address details. Teardown releases that context when no events remain allocated.

The ITS interrupt domain publishes allocation and release plus activation and deactivation operations together with a library selection helper. Allocation reserves event identifiers and parent interrupts and installs per interrupt state. Release undoes the reservation. Activation maps an event to its low power interrupt and deactivation removes that mapping.

The ITS message chip advertises a fixed identifier and forwards masking and unmasking plus acknowledgement and affinity and state handling to its parent. It adds a compose step that derives message data from the event portion of the hardware number and message address from the device translate base.

The wire bridge publishes a message template and a creation helper for per device domains. The template fixes chip behaviour and translation behaviour plus bus type and allocation flags. The helper fails when the device lacks a parent message domain and otherwise creates a domain of the requested size with private bridge state.
The wire bridge is provided as a platform driver with a fixed driver name and open firmware and ACPI match entries plus a probe routine. User initiated binding is suppressed.

Boottime ACPI handling provides one parser for translator entries and one parser plus one cleanup routine for translate frames. The translator parser brings up a controller instance. The translate parser registers per frame message tokens and the cleanup routine deregisters them.
A firmware node helper builds a parented domain token from a physical address and a parent handle using the real chip node flavour.

Bridge private state holds a mapped register base and a count of register groups. All wire enable and type accesses derive a group index and bit position from the wire number and operate at base plus group offset.

ITS device state as observed across uses holds a device identifier and an event count plus a back link to its controller and a bitmap of event use and a translate base address. Creation initialises these members and lookup and allocation and message building consume them.

A per controller device allocation lock serialises creation and destruction of device contexts including lookup insertion and removal and bitmap allocation and release. Prepare and teardown each hold this guard across their full body.
Device identifiers are unique per controller. Lookup returns the stored context for a known identifier and creation fails when the identifier already exists so duplicates never enter the lookup.
Teardown requires that no event bits remain set. When the bitmap is not empty the path warns and returns early leaving lookup entry and bitmap and registration untouched.

Table mapping is single shot per event. Mapping fails when the entry already carries a valid marking. Unmapping clears the valid marking. Both paths store the updated entry and invalidate cached table state for that device and event.

The hardware number jointly encodes device identity and event identity. Message composition reads the event portion for message data. Allocation installs the packed value while release and activation and deactivation extract the event portion from it.

Event allocation supports dynamic search and fixed reservation. Dynamic search finds a free aligned region sized for the request. Fixed reservation requires a single interrupt and checks table bounds and prior occupancy before recording the base.

Domain allocation installs per interrupt state with single target delivery and affinity applied at activation time using a fast acknowledgement handler. Platform message preparation and parent allocation precede installation and event range release follows early failure.
Domain release frees the event bitmap range and resets each interrupt datum and frees the parent hierarchy. Controller and system synchronisation steps run after the hierarchy is freed.
Wire addressing uses a fixed group size with the group index from division and the bit from remainder. Indices beyond the configured group count are rejected for both enable control and type control.
Trigger type handling sets the per wire type bit for level signalling and clears it for edge signalling. Other trigger modes are rejected without touching hardware.

Firmware translation needs at least two parameters and keeps only the sense portion of the type parameter. Open firmware reads the wire number directly while ACPI firmware extracts a wire subfield from the first parameter.

Bridge initialisation derives total wire count and group count from an identification register and requires a firmware enabled control bit. It then clears every enable group and waits for idle before creating the device domain.

Translator bringup reserves the control window and allocates a domain token and records the entry under scan and processes linked translate frames and maps registers and initialises bases with coherency derived from entry flags. Failure at any stage unwinds earlier stages in reverse order.

Translate frame handling ignores frames not linked to the entry under scan. Matching frames allocate a parented token and register it under the frame identifier. Cleanup finds the token by frame identifier and deregisters and frees it.
Descriptor installation records the message descriptor and derives the hardware number from a cookie value stored in the descriptor.
Low power identifier management fails allocation when no identifiers are configured and otherwise allocates within the configured bound. Release returns the identifier to the pool.
Private peripheral priority setup writes a repeated middle priority pattern to every priority register and then issues a synchronisation barrier so later execution observes the new values.

Device context lifecycle starts absent and moves to present with lookup entry and bitmap and registration on prepare. It stays present while events exist and returns to absent on teardown only when the event bitmap is empty.

Event lifecycle moves from free to allocated on domain allocation and to mapped on activation and back to allocated on deactivation and to free on domain release. Mapping binds the event to a low power interrupt and unmapping clears the binding.

Wire enable lifecycle performs a read modify write of the enable group followed by a wait for idle status. Enable sets the wire bit and disable clears it. Interrupt level enable and disable combine the wire update with the matching parent operation.

Probe lifecycle acquires a memory resource and maps it and initialises bridge bases and clears firmware dependencies. Base initialisation allocates state and validates identification and firmware enablement and clears enables and creates the device domain.

Translator bringup lifecycle advances through reservation and token allocation and translate scan and mapping and base initialisation. Any failure unwinds through unmapping and translate deregistration and token release and region release.

Message prepare and teardown serve as lifecycle entry points for device contexts. Prepare receives domain and device and vector count with allocation info. Teardown receives domain with allocation info.

Domain allocation and release with activation and deactivation serve as lifecycle entry points for event interrupts. Allocation and release receive domain with interrupt range details. Activation and deactivation receive domain with interrupt data.

Bridge enable and disable with type setting serve as entry points for wire control. Enable and disable receive interrupt data. Type setting additionally receives a trigger mode and programs the type register.
ACPI parsers and platform probe serve as boot and bind entry points. Parsers receive a table header with an end bound during table walks. Probe runs when a matching device is found.

Duplicate device registration and duplicate table mapping and teardown with live events and fixed reservation outside bounds or on an occupied bit risk lookup or table or bitmap corruption. Each condition is rejected through an error or warning path.

Invalid wire indices and unexpected trigger types and missing parent message domains and firmware disabled bridge state risk silent misconfiguration. Each condition fails with diagnostics before hardware is trusted.
Translator bringup can encounter busy regions and token or mapping failures and translate registration failures. Correct handling requires unwinding all previously acquired resources to avoid leaks.
Exhaustion of low power identifiers must be reported as allocation failure and never used as a valid interrupt identity.
A dedicated constant defines the ITS control window length used for reservation and mapping. It denotes a sixty four kilobyte sized region.
The private peripheral count is one hundred twenty eight.
The interrupt priority mask value is thirty one with a default of five priority bits. A middle priority value is derived by masking the priority mask.
Wire control groups each cover thirty two wires. Total wire count is a multiple of this group size derived from identification state.

The ITS message chip advertises GICv5-ITS-MSI and the wire bridge chip advertises GICv5-IWB. The bridge platform driver uses name GICv5 IWB with open firmware compatible arm,gic-v5-iwb and ACPI identifier ARMH0003.
